articles.title: Saipem and MDC sign MoU for offshore drilling in Egypt
articles.description: Saipem and Modern Drilling Company (MDC) have entered into a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to assess new collaboration opportunities in offshore drilling, beginning in the Egyptian market.

articles.title: Cheniere signs LNG supply deals with QatarEnergy through 2054
articles.description: Cheniere Energy has signed long-term sale and purchase agreements (SPAs) with QatarEnergy for the supply of a combined total of four million tonnes per annum (mtpa) of liquefied natural gas (LNG) through to 2054.

articles.title: Equinor and partners award Wisting FEED contract to Aibel
articles.description: Equinor and its partners have awarded Aibel a contract to carry out front-end engineering and design (FEED) for the topsides of the production vessel at the Wisting oil discovery in the Barents Sea.

articles.title: U.S. Partner in Venezuela Oil Deal Looks to Hike Crude Production
articles.description: The privately held company that’s partnering with the U.S. Administration to boost oil production in Venezuela has raised output by about 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) since August and plans to soon add more rigs to further hike production. North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), announced by the White House in August as one of the U.S. Administration’s partners in “the biggest oil deal in world history”, will soon activate three rigs in the fields it now operates, doubling the number of active rigs in its projects,…

articles.title: Oil Prices Hold Near $100 as Middle East Risks Offset Peace Hopes
articles.description: December WTI crude oil is nearly unchanged for the week, but the flat result hides a rough ride. The contract opened at $99.04, rallied to $101.37, then broke to $95.25 before recovering back to its opening level. At 00:19 GMT, December WTI crude oil is trading at $99.29, up $0.25 or +0.25% for the week. The high matched the June contract high. The low came on peace-talk headlines. Neither side won the week. Buyers could not hold the breakout, but sellers could not keep the market under pressure after the break. The Peace-Talk Trade Did Not Stick…

articles.title: Why Smart Investors Are Selling Oil Stocks and Buying MLPs
articles.description: It is often said that a very high percentage of individuals who trade in their own investment or brokerage accounts go broke within the first year. articles.title: Egypt Moves to Defend Saudi Arabia as Iran War Threatens to Widen
articles.description: Saudi Arabia was already the most exposed country in the US-Iran war, and Iran has now explicitly listed Saudi refineries, data centers, and undersea communications cables as the next targets should Washington strike again. articles.title: Renewables Boom Pushes Australia’s Gas Power to Quarter-Century Low
articles.description: Record renewable power generation and a surge in grid-scale battery capacity pushed Australia’s gas-powered generation to its lowest for any third quarter since 2000, the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) said in its Quarterly Energy Dynamics (QED) report on Friday. Despite lower heating requirements, Australia’s electricity demand rose by 1.3% in the July-September winter quarter, amid ongoing electrification, higher industrial demand, and increasing data center consumption, AEMO said. “Electricity use…

articles.title: How Elon Musk’s SpaceX Became a Gatekeeper of Modern Warfare
articles.description: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict On October 13, Ukrainian drones began falling out of the sky after SpaceX imposed new restrictions on the satellite connections that control them. Some lost contact with their operators when they reached 90 km/hour; others had to fly slowly enough to remain connected, making them easier targets for Russian air defenses. Ukraine also lost the ability to use some of its interceptor drones against Russian attacks. CBS News and the Wall Street Journal claim Musk personally ordered the restrictions, while Reuters…

articles.title: European Natural Gas Prices Surge to Highest Level Since 2022
articles.description: The benchmark European natural gas price jumped by 3% at opening in Amsterdam on Friday as the Middle East escalation continues to restrict Qatari LNG flows and some EU countries started tapping gas in storage as temperatures drop. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, jumped by 3% at 7 a.m. Amsterdam time on Friday, as oil prices also rose, and Brent hit a five-month high of $114 per barrel as concerns grow that Houthi attacks could hit Saudi Arabian energy facilities. articles.title: Eni's Profits Soar 125% as Refining Boom Fuels Massive Investor Payouts
articles.description: Italian energy group Eni is boosting its payout to investors with an extraordinary dividend and increased share buybacks after more than doubling its third-quarter earnings on higher oil and gas production and soaring refining margins. Eni’s adjusted net profit more than doubled from a year earlier to $3.14 billion (2.8 billion euros) for the third quarter, driven by higher oil and gas production and realizations and more than doubled refining margins across its operations, the Italian company said on Friday. The profit topped consensus estimates…

articles.title: UK Rules Out Winter Energy Shortages as Gas Prices Soar
articles.description: There is no risk of power or gas outages during this winter in the UK, as there will be sufficient generation and gas supply, the National Energy System Operator has said in its early winter outlook. In fact, NESO said it expected surplus electricity output at 5.5 GW for the period between October 31 and March 31 next year, “with an 8.8% buffer over expected peak demand.” Things may yet change, however, the grid operator also said, noting factors to watch such as electricity generation in continental Europe, gas market developments,…

articles.title: Japan Weighs Gasoline Subsidy Cuts as Energy Costs Soar
articles.description: The Japanese government may start reducing its financial support for retail gasoline prices from December as payments become difficult to sustain, Reuters has reported, citing unnamed sources from the ruling party in the country. Introduced in March, soon after the war in the Middle East began, subsidies for gasoline are costing Tokyo several billion dollars every month, the report said, as the government aimed to keep the average national price at $1.09 per liter. According to plans currently being discussed by the government and the ruling party,…

articles.title: Brent Hits $114 as Houthi Attacks Threaten Saudi Energy Infrastructure
articles.description: Crude oil prices were on course to book a sharp weekly gain, with Brent crude on track for gains of about $6 per barrel and WTI registering a much more modest tick higher, from around $99 per barrel on Monday to over $100 earlier today. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $114.00 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was changing hands for $100.40 per barrel, as hostilities in the Middle East remain front-page news for oil traders. The focus, however, seems to be on Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including Aramco facilities.…

articles.title: Why Trump Can't Afford to Lose The Rare Earth Race
articles.description: For years, the West has searched for a technological escape hatch from rare earths. Engineers have developed new motor designs, alternative magnet chemistries, and materials that reduce or even eliminate the need for some critical minerals. Every time China tightens export controls, those efforts receive another burst of attention. They're worth pursuing. But they don't answer the question manufacturers have to solve today. Production capacity has become the number one scarce asset. That realization is driving one of the most ambitious industrial…

articles.title: China's Petrochemicals Glut Turns to Crunch
articles.description: China has burned through much of a petrochemicals glut built up by years of overproduction as the U.S.-Iran war chokes oil flows.

articles.title: Oil Surges 4% After Deadly Saudi Attacks
articles.description: Brent climbed above $113 amid Saudi attacks and renewed Iran tensions, while global diesel supplies remained tight.

articles.title: LNG Canada Doubles Capacity as Asia Looks Beyond the Gulf
articles.description: Last month, Shell (NYSE:SHEL), alongside Malaysia's PETRONAS, China's PetroChina, Mitsubishi Corporation and KOGAS, officially approved the Final Investment Decision (FID) for the LNG Canada Phase 2 expansion project, doubling the facility's capacity to 28 million tons per annum (mtpa) and reinforcing the country's potential as a significant long-term supplier to Asian markets. articles.title: Rising Crude Oil Imports Reduce China’s Need to Draw from Stocks
articles.description: China has relied on its huge crude oil inventories since the Iran war hiked oil prices to above $100 per barrel. The world’s biggest crude importer has drawn from its 1.3-billion-barrel stash for most of the months after March as it slashed imports amid soaring prices. The stock draws, and the reduced imports in the spring and summer, have even kept benchmark crude oil prices in check despite the major disruption to flows from the Middle East, as China’s crude supply management was one of the key buffers the market has had since the…

articles.title: EU’s Arctic Strategy Excludes Oil and Gas
articles.description: The European Union will shun crude oil and natural gas produced from fields in the Arctic, recommending that these “stay in the ground” under its new Arctic strategy released this week. The reiteration of the EU’s stance on Arctic hydrocarbons comes amid a severe fuel crisis and soaring gas prices ahead of winter peak demand season. The update on the Arctic strategy of the bloc that has quite limited geographical exposure to the Arctic comes five years after the last one, as the Arctic draws increasing attention, notably from…

articles.title: APA makes FID on $492m Bulloo Interlink Pipeline in Australia
articles.description: APA Group has made a FID to build the interstate BIL project in Australia, committing $492m to its construction and commissioning.
